name: American Trench
why: Philadelphia clothing made in the US since 2013: heavyweight tees, knits, socks and the Ventile trench coat, sold from its own site, a store in Ardmore and specialty shops.
origin: Founded in 2013 in Philadelphia by Jacob Hurwitz and David Neill.

cities: One store, in Ardmore · its own site, and independent shops

craft_evidence.owned: NONE: About page says it works with domestic manufacturers; no owned factory stated
craft_evidence.makers: Better Team USA (New Jersey, outerwear) on Ventile Barn Coat page; Green Matters Natural Dye Company (Pennsylvania, hand dyeing); other makers described but not named ("established Pennsylvania factory since the 1980s", "tailoring factory in New England", "New York knitwear factory", LA garment district)
craft_evidence.mills: Halley Stevensons (waxed cotton, UK); Abraham Moon (UK); American Woolen (Connecticut, since 1853); Magee 1866 (Ireland); Baird McNutt (Ireland); Subalpino (Italy); Pontetorto (Italy); Brisbane Moss (UK); Nihon Menpu (Japan); Ventile (Switzerland)
craft_evidence.madein: 101 of 102 non-footwear men's product pages state US making (97 say "Made in the USA"); the Material and Factory panels carry origin on every page read; read from all 102 pages 2026-10-24
craft_evidence.heritage: Partial: About page says Philadelphia-based, no founding date; product copy says the trench coat was introduced in 2013 (and elsewhere "over 15 years later", which does not fit 2013)
craft_evidence.process: Partly: vintage low-gauge knitting machine, hand-dipped natural indigo at Green Matters, whole-garment and fully-fashioned knitting named; "Words from the Knitter" notes on some pages
craft_evidence.reasoning: Every product page carries Material and Factory panels with a stated US origin, and named mills (Abraham Moon, American Woolen, Magee, Baird McNutt, Pontetorto, Nihon Menpu) appear on the pages, plus two named makers/dyers. The brand owns no factory it states, and most factories are described, not named, so it sits at a named-makers-and-mills 3, not a 4. Sebastian rules.

ownership.owner: Privately held by its founders, Jacob Hurwitz and David Neill.

opview: “We believe manufacturing is more than the final step in making a garment. It is part of the garment itself.” — American Trench, house voice, American Trench, About Us page
